design_critique: 1) Sensor coverage holes are created by the proposed pitch. The footprint is 16 mm and the pitch is 40 mm, leaving 24 mm gaps. The tape is 25 mm wide, so the tape can sit between two footprints. At a tape-centre offset near 0.02 m, sensors at 0 and 0.04 each overlap the tape by only about 0.5 mm, so the sum of readings is near the 0.05 line-loss threshold. The rationale says the 0.04 m spacing keeps adjacent sensors overlapping the tape, which the geometry does not support. Iteration 5 used a 30 mm pitch, which closes these gaps. Line-loss events could therefore rise, not fall. 2) The outer sensors at x = +/-0.08 read tape only when the tape centre is more than about 0.06 m off (0.08 - 0.0205). The off-track limit is 0.06 m, so these two sensors contribute only once the robot has already left the allowed band. They add no information about the 0.06 m excursion that ends every run. Their weights of +/-2 also make the signal jump when they start reading, which changes the effective gain the rationale assumes. 3) The rationale's own mechanism does not match the evidence. max_error is pinned at 0.061 to 0.063 on every track, and rms_error is flat at about 0.03. Line-loss events are already 0.0 to 0.1 on the oval and 0.0 on the s-bend in iteration 5, so the line-loss term in the score (120*(1 - loss/8)) has almost no headroom to gain. 4) The y = 0.08 placement puts the sensors 1.5 cm ahead of the body front edge (length 0.14 gives a front at y = 0.07). This is inside the contract limit but outside the body, which the draft does not mention and which may not be physically meaningful. 5) The draft proposes no way to separate the sensing change from the lead change: both move together, so a result cannot be attributed to either. 6) The design does not address the constant offset pattern (flat rms, max_error at the limit on every track). A steady offset would not be fixed by wider sensors.
rationale_critique: 1) The central claim, that span is the limit, is asserted rather than shown. The rationale does not say why the wider span should prevent a failure that occurs at 0.06 m, a distance the outer sensors cannot read until the robot is already off track. 2) The expected result (progress above 0.55, fewer line-loss events) has no magnitude and no uncertainty. The line-loss gain is nearly zero because the baseline is already 0 to 0.1 on two tracks. 3) The tape-coverage argument is wrong in its arithmetic (see design critique point 1), so the stated reason for the 0.04 spacing does not hold. 4) The decision rule is incomplete. It covers the case 'max_error still reaches 0.06 with the same rms' (test lower kp with larger kd), but iteration 4 already showed that raising kd did not reduce oscillation or excursions, so that test is unlikely to succeed. It gives no rule for the case where line-loss rises, which the coverage gap predicts. 5) It does not state how the speed-related completion term is handled. At base_speed 1.3 the 1.88 s oval finish shows time is not binding there, but the rationale defers completion to later without a time estimate for the s-bend or slalom. 6) The rationale does not address the identical-metric problem from iterations 2, 4, 5 to 8, which may mean some fields are not changing the simulator output. A test that confirms the sensor change reaches the race output (for example, a changed metric at four decimals) should be stated.
